items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee addresses the interviewer as 'Helen' multiple times (e.g., 'As I say Helen...', 'Well actually what happened Helen was...'). The person to judge is 'Helen Armstead Johnston'. There is no evidence in the transcript that the interviewee (Jimmy McPartland) knows Helen Armstead Johnston

ctx.x: But gospel music involved improvisation of the music itself too. Yes. Which is the clerical side of jazz.
As I say Helen, that was my brother and myself our first contact with what we call jazz now. Those eight blind men singing spirituals.

One of the reasons I said do you think, asked you whether that group was a negro group or not was that I have observed with the now jazz workshops that are being held in the various colleges around the Country. And Stan Kenton for example is perhaps the person most in demand for giving these jazz workshops. And the purpose of them is supposed to be to teach young people, particularly young white people, about jazz.
